Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Auto rickshaw Nagarathna.H.S vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68392915/
1 bearing No.KA-01-AD-2118 asserting that on 31.10.2022 at about 8.00 a.m. when walking on the service road, near entrance of the KSRTC bus stand within the limits of Upparapete Police Station,
Bengaluru, driver of Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AD- 2118, drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi hospital, Bengaluru and ESI Hospital, Rajajinagar,
Bengaluru.
As on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 54 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/p.m. by working as Home Keeper.

3. Regarding accident Upparpet traffic police, Bengaluru registered crime No.112/2021 against the driver of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AD-2118.
4.

In response to the notice, respondents appeared through their Advocates, filed separate written statement, denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation, income,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

5. On the basis of the pleadings on 17.04.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 31.10.2022 at about 8.00 a.m. near KSRTC service road entrance, Bengaluru, she met with an accident and sustained injuries,
was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Auto Rickshaw bearing registration NO.KA-01-AD-2118 as alleged?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
6. On 12.10.2023, 14.03.2024 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 16 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.16.

On 18.04.2024, 06.07.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of Manjunath Patil -Medical Record officer at ESI Hospital and Dr. S.A. Somashekara as PW2 and PW3 and get produced 7 documents at Ex.P.17 to P.23.
7.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioner and respondent No.1-insurance company and perused the records.

8. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues and additional issue are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.2,56,376/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from 31.07.2023 as compensation from the respondents.

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 31.10.2022 at about 8.00 a.m. when walking on the service road, near entrance of the KSRTC bus stand within the limits of Upparapete Police Station, Bengaluru, driver of Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AD-2118, drove the same negligently,
dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.

10. In the written statement respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident and asserted that negligent crossing of the road by the petitioner, the accident taken place.
11. In the cross-examination petitioner/PW.1 denied the suggestion that on the date of accident she was crossing the road and explained that she already crossed the road and standing on the divider.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that in the sketch it has been shown that the accident taken place on the road.
PW.1 admitted that in the place of accident many persons will be crossing the road.
Petitioner admitted that she intended to cross the road if there has been no vehicles on the road.
Petitioner stated that prior to the accident she has not seen the auto rickshaw.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that she made attempt to cross the road without observing movement of the auto rickshaw,
therefore, she met with an accident.

12. In the evidence PW.2- Medical Record Assistant of ESI Hospital produced copy of MLC extract,
police intimation at Ex.P.18 and P.19.
13.
In the cross-examination PW.2 submitted ignorance to the suggestion that in Ex.P.18 and P.19 the number of the vehicle which caused the accident is not mentioned.
14. In the evidence PW.3- Dr. S.A. Somashekhara stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.

15. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR with complaint pertaining to crime No.112/2022 registered by Upparpet Traffic police against driver of Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AD-2118 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC, Sec.134(B) r/w Sec.187 of MV Act regarding the accident taken place on 31.10.2022 at 8.00 a.m. resulting in the injuries to the petitioner, on the basis of the complaint presented by B.S. Hiriyanna S/o Late Sathyanarayana husband of the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of sketch of the place of accident.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P5 is the copy of the motor vehicle accident report.

Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate issued by Sreenivasa Hospital, Bengaluru in which reason for the injuries suffered by the petitioner is noted as "when patient was crossing the road near Majestic bus stand, Amar junction at 7.40 a.m. on 31.10.2022 hit by auto".

Ex.P7 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Upparpet traffic police in crime No.112/2022 against respondent No.2 Harish Kumar S/o Krishnappa driver of Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AD-2118 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,
337, 338 of IPC and Sec.134(B) r/w sec.187 of MV Act.
In Ex.P.18

3 Medical College and Hospital and Ex.

P.19 Police intimation dated 03.11.2022 sent by Chief Medical Officer, ESI Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru the reason for the injuries suffered by the petitioner is noted as RTA while patient was walking out from metro station, autorickshaw hit from back on 31.10.2022 at 8.15 a.m. near Majestic metro station, Tank Bund road, Majestic, patient complained pain and swelling on right lower limb, patient initially taken to Sreenivasa Hospital by public, then patient shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Trauma Orthopedics for further management.
16. In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason, mode and consequence of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 31.10.2022 at about 8.00 a.m. when petitioner was walking on the service road,
near entrance of the KSRTC bus stand within the limits of Upparapete Police Station, Bengaluru,
respondent No.2- Hareesh K. driver of Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA- 01-AD-2118, drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident she has suffered fracture of right hip, fracture of right femur inter trochantric and injuries all over the body, took first aid/treatment at Sanjay Gandhi hospital, Bengaluru, ESI Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru as inpatient and underwent surgery by spending Rs.1,00,000/-, as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.25,000/-p.m. by working as House Keeper.
18. In the written statement, respondent No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
19. In the cross-examination, petitioner stated that immediately after the accident she was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital and then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital.
Petitioner stated about taking of treatment as inpatient for the period of 4 days at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital.
Petitioner stated that at ESI Hospital she was taken treatment as inpatient for 15 days.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that she never underwent surgery to right lower limb.
Petitioner denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment and requirement of Rs.50,000/- for further treatment.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that she was not having income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
20. In the evidence PW.2- Medical Record Assistant at ESI Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru produced OPD card, copy of MLC register extract, case sheet and X-rays.

21. In the evidence affidavit PW.3 Dr. S.A. Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital stated that on 13.12.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 38% to right lower limb which is about 19% to the whole body.
In the evidence PW.3 produced OPD record and X-ray at Ex.P.22 and P.23.
In the cross-examination PW.3 admitted that he never treated the petitioner, only to assess the disability on 13.12.2023 clinically examined the petitioner.
PW.3 stated that as on 13.12.2023 fractures of the petitioner are united.

sentences.text:
Wound certificate, discharge summary, OPD slips prescriptions, medical bills, case sheet, X-ray and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered fracture of right femur/right intertrochanteric fracture, took treatment at Srinivasa Hospital, Sanjay Gandhi Hospital and ESI Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru as inpatient for the total period of 16 days then took follow- up treatment, at the cost of Rs.6,200/- (1st time) and Rs.7,126/- (2nd time).
23.
In the Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P.10 the date birth of the petitioner is noted as 18.01.1966.
There are no documents regarding occupation and income of the petitioner.
In the file there are no documents regarding decrease in the income of the petitioner or loss of income of the petitioner subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.3 Dr.S.A. Somashekara is not sufficient to award compensation under the head loss of future income(Permanent Physical Disability).
24.

Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, I award Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.6,200/-
towards medical expenses, from 03.11.2022 to 19.11.2022, Rs.7,126/- towards 2 nd time treatment taken during July-2023, Rs.25,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges,
Rs.93,000/- (Rs.15,500 x 6) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.50,000/-
towards loss of amenities and future happiness.

Hence, I come to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle to receive compensation at Rs.2,69,670/- with current and future interest at 6% per annum from 31.07.2023.
25.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.2,56,376/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from 31.07.2023 as compensation.
26. In the written statement, respondent No.1 and 2 admitted that as on the date of accident Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AD-2118 had insurance coverage with respondent No.1.
The copy of the Driving Licence No.KA05 20050005969 shows that as on the date of accident Harish Kumar had licence to drive the Cab (Auto Rickshaw).
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident respondent No.2-owner of the auto violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owner of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AD-2118 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.2,56,376/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from 31.07.2023, to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AD-2118 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
